resources.title: Product Management 101: Everything You Need to Know (Full Course)
resources.why: A single-sitting overview of what PMs do day to day. Watch it first so the rest of your learning has a map.

resources.title: How to Transition Into Product Management from Consulting
resources.why: Concrete framing for turning consulting experience into PM evidence. Useful for any analyst-type background too.

resources.title: Consulting to Product Management: How Cara Made the Transition
resources.why: A real transition story, which helps you see the sequence of steps beyond generic advice.

resources.title: I Quit Software Engineering to Become an AI PM. Here’s How
resources.why: An engineer-to-AI-PM account with a roadmap. Treat it as one person’s path, not a universal recipe.

resources.title: Y Combinator Startup Library
resources.why: Short, practical essays and videos on building products people want. Great for the founder-minded product habits.

resources.title: Digital Product Management: Modern Fundamentals
resources.why: A structured, university-backed intro with graded exercises. Audit it for free, pay only if you want the certificate.

resources.title: Reforge Courses
resources.why: Operator-taught programs on growth, strategy and product leadership. Best once you have a year or two of PM experience.

resources.title: Product School Resources
resources.why: A large library of guides, templates and talks. Use search; it’s a library, not a path.

resources.title: Continuous Discovery Habits
resources.why: The most practical book on weekly customer touchpoints and opportunity solution trees. Directly usable at work and in interviews.

resources.title: Build Better Products with Continuous Product Discovery
resources.why: Teresa Torres explains continuous discovery in conversation. A gentler on-ramp to the book.

resources.title: The Mom Test
resources.why: Short and sharp: how to ask customer questions that don’t produce polite lies. Fixes most beginner interview mistakes.

resources.title: Know Your Customers’ “Jobs to Be Done”
resources.why: The canonical article on the jobs-to-be-done lens. Pairs well with customer-interview practice.

resources.title: UX Research Cheat Sheet
resources.why: Which research method to use at which stage. Handy when an interviewer asks how you would validate an idea.

resources.title: Inspired: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love
resources.why: The foundational book on modern product teams. Read it to learn the vocabulary every PM interviewer assumes.

resources.title: Empowered: Ordinary People, Extraordinary Products
resources.why: About leading product teams and what good product leadership looks like. A strong Senior+ read.

resources.title: SVPG Articles
resources.why: Short opinionated essays on product teams, roadmaps and leadership. Read a handful to absorb the point of view.

resources.title: Marty Cagan: Strong Opinions, Loosely Held
resources.why: Marty Cagan on product practice, with strong views worth knowing even where you disagree.

resources.title: Is Shreyas Doshi Right About Avoiding “Process People”?
resources.why: A debate on product process vs. judgement. Good fuel for strategy and culture questions.

resources.title: RICE: Simple Prioritization for Product Managers
resources.why: The standard explanation of RICE scoring. Know it cold, and also know when not to use it.

resources.title: Product Roadmap: Learn Guide
resources.why: A plain-English walkthrough of what a roadmap is and the formats you’ll see in real companies.

resources.title: Roadmapping Guide
resources.why: A more detailed roadmapping guide with formats and stakeholder views.

resources.title: Product Requirements Documents (PRDs)
resources.why: A clear PRD structure with a template to start from. Adapt it, don’t copy it.

resources.title: Intercom on Product Management
resources.why: A free ebook of practical lessons from a well-known product company. Good for execution habits.

resources.title: Aggregation Theory
resources.why: A widely used lens for why some consumer platforms win. Useful vocabulary for strategy questions.

resources.title: Gibson Biddle: Product Strategy
resources.why: Lessons from a former Netflix and Chegg product leader on strategy and goals.

resources.title: The Looking Glass
resources.why: Writing on product design and management from a former Facebook design leader. Great on leading people.

resources.title: First Round Review
resources.why: Long-form interviews with operators. Search “product” for deep, quotable material.

resources.title: Casey Winters
resources.why: Growth and product leadership essays from an experienced operator.

resources.title: Product-Market Fit Guide
resources.why: A structured way to think about finding and measuring product-market fit.

resources.title: SQLBolt
resources.why: Interactive SQL lessons you can finish in a weekend. Enough SQL for most PM data questions.

resources.title: SQL Tutorial for Data Analysis
resources.why: A more analysis-oriented SQL tutorial. Follow SQLBolt with this for joins, windows and real analyses.

resources.title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments
resources.why: The reference book on A/B testing at scale. Dense, but it separates serious experimenters from the rest.

resources.title: Sample Size Calculator for A/B Tests
resources.why: A calculator you can use in the interview itself to reason about how long a test must run.

resources.title: The North Star Playbook
resources.why: How to choose a north-star metric and the input metrics beneath it. Directly useful for metrics interview questions.

resources.title: Amplitude Blog
resources.why: Product analytics articles on retention, funnels and experimentation. Browse by topic.

resources.title: AI for Everyone
resources.why: A non-technical introduction to what AI can and can’t do. A good first step before specialist AI PM material.

resources.title: Rules of Machine Learning
resources.why: Google’s best-practice guide for ML products. Teaches the product-side judgement behind ML projects.

resources.title: People + AI Guidebook
resources.why: Design and product patterns for AI features: trust, feedback, error handling. Great for AI product sense.

resources.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
resources.why: The clearest practical write-up on testing LLM features. Evals are becoming a core PM skill.

resources.title: Why AI Evals Are the Hottest New Skill for Product Builders
resources.why: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar on how to evaluate AI products. Pairs with the written guide above.

resources.title: The Most Important New Skill for PMs in 2026: AI Evals Masterclass
resources.why: A PM-oriented walkthrough of AI evals. Good for seeing what this looks like in a product role.

resources.title: From Noob to Automated Evals in a Week (as a PM)
resources.why: Teresa Torres learns evals as a PM, so the learning curve is visible. Reassuring for non-engineers.

resources.title: AI Product Management: Complete Course (3.5 hours)
resources.why: A long-form AI PM overview covering agents, RAG and evals. Good as a one-weekend primer.

resources.title: Prompt Engineering Overview
resources.why: Official guidance on prompting. Hands-on practice here makes you credible in AI product discussions.

resources.title: Building Effective Agents
resources.why: A clear taxonomy of agentic patterns and when not to use them. Useful for AI product strategy conversations.

resources.title: DeepLearning.AI (YouTube)
resources.why: Talks and short lessons on applied AI. Browse for topics you keep hearing at work.

resources.title: Andrej Karpathy (YouTube)
resources.why: Technical but clear explanations of how LLMs work. You don’t need to code along to build intuition.

resources.title: Meta PM Interview: Instagram Viewership Drop (Mock)
resources.why: A mock with a Meta PM on a classic metric-drop question. Study how they structure the diagnosis.

resources.title: Google Product Manager Mock Interview
resources.why: A full Google-style product design answer. Compare their structure with your own.

resources.title: Meta Product Sense Interview (with Meta PM)
resources.why: A Meta-style product sense walkthrough from a practising PM. Good for framework depth.

resources.title: Meta Product Sense Mock: Friend Requests Down
resources.why: An execution-style question on a falling metric. Practise pausing the video and answering first.

resources.title: Product Sense Mock: Fitness App for Meta
resources.why: A design-style mock with ex-Instagram and ex-Uber PMs. Shows how interviewers push back.

resources.title: Creative Product Sense Mock Interview
resources.why: Focuses on generating creative solutions. Useful when your answers feel formulaic.

resources.title: Aced (formerly Exponent)
resources.why: Courses, question bank and mock interviews for PM roles. Strong content, but pricing and plans change, so check the site.

resources.title: Lewis C. Lin
resources.why: Author of well-known PM interview books and frameworks. Browse his articles for question types.

resources.title: Aced / Exponent (YouTube channel)
resources.why: The largest free collection of PM mock interviews. Pick by company and question type.

resources.title: Lenny’s Podcast
resources.why: Long conversations with product leaders. The best way to learn how senior PMs actually think.

resources.title: Lenny’s Newsletter
resources.why: The most-read PM newsletter. Search the archive for career, growth and AI topics.

resources.title: Product Growth
resources.why: Practical PM career and AI PM guides, resume and interview content included.

resources.title: The Product Compass
resources.why: Hands-on posts on AI product work, discovery and strategy.

resources.title: Mind the Product
resources.why: Articles, conference talks and a community around product management.

resources.title: Reforge Blog
resources.why: Frameworks on growth, product strategy and careers from operators.

resources.title: Nielsen Norman Group Articles
resources.why: Evidence-based UX writing. Use it to back product-sense answers with research.

resources.title: Levels.fyi
resources.why: Compensation data by company and level, US and India. Use it to benchmark offers before you negotiate.

resources.title: Wellfound (startup jobs)
resources.why: Startup job listings with salary and equity ranges. A strong channel for first PM roles.

paths.title: Break into PM in 8 weeks
paths.blurb: For aspiring PMs and career switchers. Learn the job, build proof, then apply.

paths.title: PM interview crash course
paths.blurb: Two weeks to a structured, confident interview performance.

paths.title: Become an AI PM in 6 weeks
paths.blurb: Build the fluency to speak credibly about AI products and evals.

paths.title: Data & experimentation for PMs
paths.blurb: Four weeks to read, query and reason about data like a product owner.

paths.title: From PM to Senior PM
paths.blurb: For PMs with 2+ years who want scope, strategy and influence.
